item.title: The Other Way to Reduce Government Debt
item.description: Financial repression.

item.title: Iran’s Oil Terminals Look Idle as US Keeps Up Naval Blockade
item.description: Iran’s oil terminals have appeared largely idle this month as the US continues to impose a blockade aimed at pressuring the country into a peace deal, though visibility into its operations remains patchy.

item.title: Ex-Intel CEO Gives Distressed Christian College $2 Million Loan
item.description: William Jessup University, a struggling Christian institution outside of Sacramento, received a lifeline from a wealthy benefactor with longstanding ties to the college.

item.title: Braskem Creditors Seek Petrobras Capital as Deal Deadline Looms
item.description: Braskem’s bondholders continue to press state-controlled oil giant Petrobras to inject fresh capital into the struggling petrochemical producer as time runs short to avoid filing for bankruptcy protection in an election year, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: EY Launching Unit to Keep a Lid on Artificial Intelligence Costs
item.description: EY is hiring a head of “agent economics” to oversee the growing ranks of its AI-powered workforce, in a sign that white-collar companies are increasing scrutiny on whether their investments in AI technology are justifying the huge cost.

item.title: Investors Abandon Hedges in Order to Chase Soaring Stocks
item.description: Demand for protection against a drop in stocks has fallen to the lowest level since US President Donald Trump’s capitulation on tariffs last year, as indexes rally to record highs.

item.title: SEC Exempts Data-Center Bonds From Key Securitization Rules
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission has made it easier for data center owners to sell asset-backed securities, potentially opening the door for more debt sales as tech firms scour Wall Street for ways to pay for artificial intelligence.

item.title: IBM Turns to Canadian Bond Market for First Time Since 2012
item.description: International Business Machines Corp. is in Canada’s bond market for the first time in 14 years, the latest entrant to what’s been a record year of issuance by foreign firms.

item.title: JPMorgan Leads $441 Million Debt Deal for AI Infrastructure Firm
item.description: Global AI, a two-year-old tech firm, has raised $441 million in debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. to meet growing demand for artificial intelligence data centers.

item.title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda Taps Loans for Nvidia-Tied Chip Deal
item.description: Lambda Inc., an AI cloud-computing provider backed by Nvidia Corp., is selling a leveraged loan to finance a chip deal as the risky debt market becomes a new front in the borrowing binge to finance the artificial intelligence buildout.

item.title: Warsh Says He Sold All Promised Stakes, Agency Filing Shows
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says he has sold all of the financial holdings he promised to divest from, a government record showed.

item.title: French Trader Sucden Warns of Sugar Oversupply as Futures Rally
item.description: The global sugar market is oversupplied, and the outlook for investors is being blurred by a lack of data, according to French trader Sucres et Denrees SA.

item.title: Energy Veteran Peter Abdo to Lead UK’s Grain LNG From October
item.description: Grain LNG, which has the largest capacity to import liquefied natural gas into the UK, has appointed Peter Abdo as its chief executive officer starting October.

item.title: Imperial Brands to Cut Thousands of Jobs in US and Europe
item.description: Imperial Brands Plc is preparing to slash thousands of jobs in critical markets, including the US and Europe, as part of a sweeping cost-cutting drive, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Natural Gas Surges as Hotter Outlooks Trigger Short-Covering
item.description: US natural gas futures rose by the most in more than two months as an unusually large swing in weather forecasts triggered a wave of short-covering among money managers who were the most bearish on gas since 2020.

item.title: Glencore Consortium Offers Rival Bid for Troubled Canadian Miner
item.description: A consortium including Glencore Plc proposed a rescue deal for troubled Canadian miner Sherritt International Corp., offering a potential alternative to an earlier plan from an ally of US President Donald Trump.

item.title: US Stocks Open Flat as Focus Turns to Chipmaker Earnings, CPI
item.description: US stocks were little changed at market open on Monday as investors gear up for the final stretch of earnings. Earnings this week from chipmakers could provide confirmation for the long-winded debate over chip valuations.

item.title: Microsoft Plans Production Boost for AI Chips, Information Says
item.description: Microsoft Corp. is planning to “significantly” increase production of its next-generation AI chips, the Information reported.

item.title: Strategy Sells More Bitcoin, Stock to Bolster Cash Stockpile
item.description: Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc. spent another week revising the company’s capital structure by selling more Bitcoin and common shares to bolster its cash reserve.

item.title: Kenya Plans Corn Imports After Crop Failure Due to Bad Weather
item.description: Kenya plans to import one million 90-kilogram bags of corn to replenish national reserves after a failed crop, according to Agriculture Secretary Mutahi Kagwe.

item.title: Anthropic, Macquarie and GIC Form Venture for AI Data Centers
item.description: Anthropic PBC has formed a strategic partnership with Macquarie Asset Management and Singaporean wealth fund GIC to build data centers for the Claude developer.

item.title: Hassett Hopes Cook Innocent, Rules Out Taking Her Place at Fed
item.description: White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said he hoped Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook is right in saying she’s innocent of mortgage fraud, while ruling out replacing her on the US central bank’s board.

item.title: Romania Keeps EU’s Highest Rates as Political Woes Cloud Outlook
item.description: Romania held interest rates at the highest level in the European Union, with the central bank waiting for inflation to slow below 10% and political turmoil to subside before considering policy easing.

item.title: Apple Cut at Jefferies on iPhone Worries as Sell Ratings Pile Up
item.description: Apple Inc. was downgraded to an underperform rating at Jefferies, in the latest example of growing bearishness toward the company.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stock Valuations Sink Below Half of S&P 500’s
item.description: For the first time in at least two decades, emerging-market stock valuations have fallen to less than half those of US equities, a sign to some investors that there are increasingly attractive opportunities in developing economies.

item.title: Intel Selling $15 Billion in Common Stock as AI Demand Booms
item.description: Intel Corp. said it will be offering $15 billion in common stock, taking advantage of renewed interest in its business prospects during the artificial intelligence data center boom.

item.title: Cloudflare Seeks to Sell $2.175 Billion in Convertible Notes
item.description: Cloudflare Inc. announced plans for a private offering of $2.175 billion of senior convertible notes, after the cybersecurity firm’s guidance boost last week sent shares to an intraday high.

item.title: Trump’s Low-Key Pivot Leaves Hormuz Oil in Limbo
item.description: The US President is betting he can wait Iran out, prolonging uncertainty for oil markets.

item.title: Unitree’s Shanghai IPO 5,526 Times Subscribed by Retail Buyers
item.description: The highly anticipated initial public offering of Yushu Technology Co., known as Unitree Robotics, drew huge demand from retail investors as China’s leading humanoid robot maker opened books in Shanghai.

item.title: Duke Energy Seeks $1.75 Billion in Equity Units Offering
item.description: Duke Energy Corp. plans to raise about $1.75 billion by selling equity units, in an effort to pay down debt.
